correctness.rationale: The exact control-to-state operator is \(K\), adjoint propagation gives the error map \(-3K^*K\), and the eigenvalue problem reduces to \(f''+(1/\mu-1)f=0\) with \(f'(0)+f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=0\). The eigenpair \((\mu,f)=(1,1-t)\) is checked directly. No \(\mu>1\) exists because it would require \(\tanh\beta=\beta\) for \(\beta>0\). Remaining eigenvalues come from \(\tan k=k\) and tend to zero. Functional calculus for compact self-adjoint \(A=K^*K\) then gives the exact norm \(\max(|1-\omega|,|1-4\omega|)\), from which the stability and minimax statements follow. The finite script only replays algebra/numerics; it is not used as an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The result resolves a concrete qualitative anomaly in a standard convergence paper: the formal unrelaxed continuous sweep is not merely noncontractive but has an exact factor-3 unstable mode, while the half-relaxed boundary creates precisely the neutral alternating mode canceled by pair averaging. The exact iff stability range and unique \(2/5\) rate-optimal relaxation provide a reusable benchmark for FBSM stabilization and distinguish formal-algorithm behavior from relaxation-induced cycling. This is a motivated boundary/tuning fact, not an arbitrary scalar slice.
